commands.name: KEYS
commands.summary: Return every key matching the glob pattern (cross-shard gather).
commands.complexity: O(N) keys in the whole keyspace — every shard walks its entire map, plus an O(P*K) glob match per key

commands.name: RANDOMKEY
commands.summary: Return a random key from the keyspace.
commands.complexity: O(1) expected — each shard probes a random slot, and the origin folds the candidates through a reservoir weighted by shard key counts, so every key is equally likely

commands.name: SCAN
commands.summary: Sweep the keyspace and return every match at once; NOT a cursor iterator (COUNT and TYPE are accepted and ignored, and the cursor is always 0).
commands.complexity: O(N) keys in the WHOLE keyspace, on every call — there is no incremental walk
commands.compat: differs: SCAN is not a cursor iterator. Every call sweeps every shard's entire keyspace and replies with cursor 0 and all matches in one batch, so the standard SCAN loop terminates after one round trip. COUNT and TYPE are accepted and ignored; MATCH is honoured. Redis's incremental, bounded-work, rehash-tolerant guarantees do not exist here

commands.name: DEL
commands.summary: Delete one or more keys.
commands.complexity: O(N) keys, plus O(M) per key holding a collection of M elements (the drop walks the container)
commands.compat: differs: the multi-key form is split by shard and summed with no barrier, so it is not atomic across shards; the single-key form is

commands.name: EXISTS
commands.summary: Count how many of the given keys exist.
commands.complexity: O(N) keys, one O(1) probe each
commands.compat: differs: the multi-key form is gathered per shard, so the count is not a point-in-time snapshot across shards

commands.name: EXPIRE
commands.summary: Set a key's TTL in seconds (non-positive TTL deletes the key).
commands.compat: differs: the NX / XX / GT / LT condition flags are not parsed — arity is fixed at 3, so EXPIRE key seconds NX is a wrong-arity error

commands.name: EXPIREAT
commands.summary: Set a key's expiry as an absolute Unix timestamp in seconds.
commands.compat: differs: the NX / XX / GT / LT condition flags are not parsed — arity is fixed at 3

commands.name: PERSIST
commands.summary: Remove a key's TTL.

commands.name: PEXPIRE
commands.summary: Set a key's TTL in milliseconds.
commands.compat: differs: the NX / XX / GT / LT condition flags are not parsed — arity is fixed at 3

commands.name: PEXPIREAT
commands.summary: Set a key's expiry as an absolute Unix timestamp in milliseconds.
commands.compat: differs: the NX / XX / GT / LT condition flags are not parsed — arity is fixed at 3

commands.name: PTTL
commands.summary: Return a key's remaining TTL in milliseconds (-1 no TTL, -2 missing).

commands.name: RENAME
commands.summary: Rename a key, overwriting the destination (write routed at the runtime Op level).
commands.complexity: O(1) for a string value; O(M) for a collection of M elements (the entry's weight is re-derived by walking the value)
commands.compat: differs: a cross-shard rename is a non-atomic Take then Put — there is a window in which neither key is visible; co-locate the two keys with a {hashtag} for the atomic path

commands.name: RENAMENX
commands.summary: Rename a key only if the destination does not exist (write routed at the runtime Op level).
commands.complexity: O(1) for a string value; O(M) for a collection of M elements
commands.compat: differs: cross-shard RENAMENX is a non-atomic Take, Put, restore-on-refusal sequence — there is a window in which the source is absent from the keyspace

commands.name: TTL
commands.summary: Return a key's remaining TTL in seconds (-1 no TTL, -2 missing).

commands.name: TYPE
commands.summary: Return the type of the value stored at key.

commands.name: UNLINK
commands.summary: Delete one or more keys (alias of DEL in kevy's shard model).
commands.complexity: O(N) keys, plus O(M) per collection-typed key — identical to DEL
commands.compat: differs: UNLINK is an alias of DEL — the value is freed inline on the owning shard's reactor thread, not by a background thread, so it gives no latency benefit

commands.name: APPEND
commands.summary: Append bytes to a string value; returns the new length.
commands.complexity: O(1) amortised while the value is <= 64 B; O(N) per call once it exceeds that (the Arc payload is copied out and re-boxed on every append), so building a large string by repeated APPEND is O(N^2)

commands.name: DECR
commands.summary: Decrement the integer value of a key by one.

commands.name: DECRBY
commands.summary: Decrement the integer value of a key by the given amount.

commands.name: GET
commands.summary: Return the string value of a key.

commands.name: GETDEL
commands.summary: Return the string value of a key and delete it.

commands.name: GETSET
commands.summary: Set a key's string value and return its previous value.

commands.name: INCR
commands.summary: Increment the integer value of a key by one.

commands.name: INCRBY
commands.summary: Increment the integer value of a key by the given amount.

commands.name: INCRBYFLOAT
commands.summary: Increment the float value of a key by the given amount.
commands.compat: differs: arithmetic is f64 and the reply uses Rust's shortest-round-trip float printer, not a long double accumulator, so trailing digits can diverge from Redis

commands.name: MGET
commands.summary: Return the values of multiple keys (cross-shard gather).
commands.complexity: O(N) keys, one O(1) probe each on the owning shard
commands.compat: differs: keys are grouped by shard and each shard is probed independently, so the reply is not a point-in-time snapshot across shards

commands.name: MSET
commands.summary: Set multiple key/value pairs atomically per shard.
commands.complexity: O(N) pairs, one O(1) SET each
commands.compat: differs: atomic only per shard — pairs are split by key and applied shard-by-shard with no cross-shard barrier, so a reader can observe some pairs written and others not; Redis MSET is globally atomic

commands.name: PSETEX
commands.summary: Set a key's value with a TTL in milliseconds.

commands.name: SET
commands.summary: Set a key's string value with optional TTL and existence conditions.
commands.compat: differs: only NX / XX / EX / PX are parsed — KEEPTTL, EXAT, PXAT, GET and the IFEQ family are a syntax error; a repeated expire option is silently accepted last-one-wins instead of erroring

commands.name: SETEX
commands.summary: Set a key's value with a TTL in seconds.

commands.name: SETNX
commands.summary: Set a key's value only if it does not exist.

commands.name: STRLEN
commands.summary: Return the length of a key's string value.

commands.name: HDEL
commands.summary: Delete one or more hash fields.
commands.complexity: O(M) fields

commands.name: HEXISTS
commands.summary: Check whether a hash field exists.

commands.name: HEXPIRE
commands.syntax: HEXPIRE key seconds [NX|XX|GT|LT] FIELDS numfields field [field ...]
commands.summary: Set per-field TTLs on a hash, in seconds.
commands.complexity: O(F) fields in the FIELDS clause
commands.compat: differs: the FIELDS parse error reads 'Mandatory keyword FIELDS is missing' where Redis says 'Mandatory argument FIELDS'

commands.name: HGET
commands.summary: Return the value of a hash field.

commands.name: HGETALL
commands.summary: Return all fields and values of a hash.
commands.complexity: O(N) fields, with a full copy of every name and value

commands.name: HINCRBY
commands.summary: Increment the integer value of a hash field.

commands.name: HKEYS
commands.summary: Return all field names of a hash.
commands.complexity: O(N) fields

commands.name: HLEN
commands.summary: Return the number of fields in a hash.

commands.name: HMGET
commands.summary: Return the values of multiple hash fields.
commands.complexity: O(M) fields requested

commands.name: HMSET
commands.summary: Deprecated alias of HSET that replies OK.
commands.complexity: O(M) pairs

commands.name: HPERSIST
commands.summary: Remove per-field TTLs from a hash.
commands.complexity: O(F) fields
commands.compat: differs: silently accepts a stray NX|XX|GT|LT token before FIELDS (it shares HEXPIRE's parser) where Redis rejects it

commands.name: HPEXPIRE
commands.syntax: HPEXPIRE key milliseconds [NX|XX|GT|LT] FIELDS numfields field [field ...]
commands.summary: Set per-field TTLs on a hash, in milliseconds.
commands.complexity: O(F) fields
commands.compat: differs: same FIELDS error-text deviation as HEXPIRE

commands.name: HPEXPIREAT
commands.syntax: HPEXPIREAT key unix-time-milliseconds [NX|XX|GT|LT] FIELDS numfields field [field ...]
commands.summary: Set per-field expiries as absolute Unix-millisecond deadlines.
commands.complexity: O(F) fields
commands.compat: differs: same FIELDS error-text deviation as HEXPIRE

commands.name: HSCAN
commands.summary: Iterate a hash's fields and values (single-batch cursor).
commands.complexity: O(N) — the whole hash is copied and returned in one batch
commands.compat: differs: not a cursor iterator — the cursor is always 0 and the entire hash comes back in a single reply; NOVALUES is not parsed and COUNT is validated then ignored

commands.name: HSET
commands.summary: Set one or more hash fields; returns the number of new fields.
commands.complexity: O(M) pairs

commands.name: HSETNX
commands.summary: Set a hash field only if it does not exist.

commands.name: HPTTL
commands.summary: Return per-field remaining TTLs in milliseconds (-1 no TTL, -2 missing).
commands.complexity: O(F) fields
commands.compat: differs: silently accepts a stray NX|XX|GT|LT token before FIELDS where Redis rejects it

commands.name: HTTL
commands.summary: Return per-field remaining TTLs in seconds (-1 no TTL, -2 missing).
commands.complexity: O(F) fields
commands.compat: differs: silently accepts a stray NX|XX|GT|LT token before FIELDS where Redis rejects it

commands.name: HVALS
commands.summary: Return all values of a hash.
commands.complexity: O(N) fields

commands.name: BLPOP
commands.summary: Blocking left pop across one or more lists (effect logged as LPOP).
commands.complexity: O(1) to serve; the park is O(1) and waiters are woken FIFO per key
commands.compat: differs: on a multi-shard server the multi-key form does not honour Redis's left-to-right key priority — keys on the connection's own shard are served before remote ones

commands.name: BRPOP
commands.summary: Blocking right pop across one or more lists (effect logged as RPOP).
commands.complexity: O(1) to serve; FIFO park
commands.compat: differs: same multi-key priority deviation as BLPOP

commands.name: BRPOPLPUSH
commands.summary: Blocking RPOPLPUSH: pop the source tail and push it onto the destination head.
commands.complexity: O(1) to serve
commands.compat: differs: a cross-shard move is not atomic — the element is popped on the source's shard and pushed on the destination's, and between those two steps it is in neither list. Co-locate the keys with a {hashtag} to get Redis's atomic path

commands.name: LINDEX
commands.summary: Return the element at the given list index.
commands.complexity: O(1) — the list is a VecDeque, so an index is a direct offset (Redis's quicklist is O(N))

commands.name: LLEN
commands.summary: Return the length of a list.

commands.name: LMOVE
commands.summary: Atomically move an element between two lists.
commands.compat: differs: a cross-shard move is not atomic — see BRPOPLPUSH

commands.name: LPOP
commands.summary: Pop one or more elements from the head of a list.
commands.complexity: O(C) elements popped
commands.compat: differs: LPOP key 0 on an existing key replies a nil array where Redis replies an empty array

commands.name: LPOS
commands.syntax: LPOS key element [RANK rank] [COUNT num-matches] [MAXLEN len]
commands.summary: Return the index of matching elements in a list.
commands.complexity: O(N) always — the whole list is copied before RANK / COUNT / MAXLEN are applied, so MAXLEN bounds the comparisons but not the copy

commands.name: LPUSH
commands.summary: Prepend one or more elements to a list.
commands.complexity: O(M) values, O(1) amortised each

commands.name: LRANGE
commands.summary: Return a range of list elements.
commands.complexity: O(M) elements returned — the start offset is skipped in O(1) (Redis is O(S+M))

commands.name: LREM
commands.summary: Remove elements equal to the given value from a list.
commands.complexity: O(N*R) worst case — the scan is O(N) but each removal shifts up to half the deque (Redis is O(N+R))

commands.name: LSET
commands.summary: Set the list element at the given index.
commands.complexity: O(1) — a direct index write (Redis is O(N) for a mid-list index)

commands.name: LTRIM
commands.summary: Trim a list to the given range.
commands.complexity: O(R) elements removed

commands.name: RPOP
commands.summary: Pop one or more elements from the tail of a list.
commands.complexity: O(C) elements popped
commands.compat: differs: RPOP key 0 on an existing key replies a nil array where Redis replies an empty array

commands.name: RPOPLPUSH
commands.summary: Pop the source tail and push it onto the destination head.
commands.compat: differs: a cross-shard move is not atomic — see BRPOPLPUSH

commands.name: RPUSH
commands.summary: Append one or more elements to a list.
commands.complexity: O(M) values, O(1) amortised each

commands.name: SADD
commands.summary: Add one or more members to a set.
commands.complexity: O(M) members

commands.name: SCARD
commands.summary: Return the number of members in a set.

commands.name: SDIFF
commands.summary: Return the difference of the given sets (cross-shard gather).
commands.complexity: O(sum of the source cardinalities)

commands.name: SDIFFSTORE
commands.summary: Store the difference of the given sets into destination.
commands.complexity: O(sum of the source cardinalities) + O(result) to write the destination on its own shard

commands.name: SINTER
commands.summary: Return the intersection of the given sets (cross-shard gather).
commands.complexity: O(sum of the source cardinalities) — there is NO smallest-set-first ordering, so SINTER huge tiny costs O(huge) where Redis costs O(tiny * k)

commands.name: SINTERSTORE
commands.summary: Store the intersection of the given sets into destination.
commands.complexity: O(sum of the source cardinalities) + O(result); same no-smallest-first algorithm

commands.name: SISMEMBER
commands.summary: Check whether a value is a member of a set.

commands.name: SMEMBERS
commands.summary: Return all members of a set.
commands.complexity: O(N) members

commands.name: SPOP
commands.summary: Remove and return one or more random members of a set.
commands.complexity: O(count) expected — each member is drawn by probing a random slot and taking the first occupied one

commands.name: SRANDMEMBER
commands.summary: Return one or more random members of a set without removing them. A negative count allows repeats.
commands.complexity: O(count) expected when count is a small fraction of the set (random-slot probing); O(N) once count exceeds a quarter of it, where copying and shuffling beats rejection sampling

commands.name: SREM
commands.summary: Remove one or more members from a set.
commands.complexity: O(M) members

commands.name: SSCAN
commands.summary: Iterate a set's members (single-batch cursor).
commands.complexity: O(N) — the whole set is copied and returned in one batch
commands.compat: differs: not a cursor iterator — the cursor is always 0 and the entire set comes back in one reply; COUNT is validated then ignored

commands.name: SUNION
commands.summary: Return the union of the given sets (cross-shard gather).
commands.complexity: O(sum of the source cardinalities)

commands.name: SUNIONSTORE
commands.summary: Store the union of the given sets into destination.
commands.complexity: O(sum of the source cardinalities) + O(result)

commands.name: BZPOPMIN
commands.summary: Blocking pop of the lowest-scored member across one or more sorted sets.
commands.complexity: O(log N) per pop; the park is O(1)

commands.name: ZADD
commands.summary: Add members with scores to a sorted set, with conditional flags.
commands.complexity: O(M log N) — O(1) hash insert plus O(log N) tree insert per member

commands.name: ZCARD
commands.summary: Return the number of members in a sorted set.

commands.name: ZCOUNT
commands.summary: Count members with scores within the given bounds.
commands.complexity: O(log N) — two rank descents on the order-statistic tree bracket the score range; nothing is scanned

commands.name: ZDIFFSTORE
commands.summary: Store the difference of the given sorted sets into destination.
commands.complexity: O(sum of the source cardinalities + R log R); each source is extracted whole on its own shard

commands.name: ZINCRBY
commands.summary: Increment a member's score in a sorted set.
commands.complexity: O(log N)

commands.name: ZINTERCARD
commands.summary: Return the cardinality of the intersection of the given sorted sets.
commands.complexity: O(sum of the source cardinalities) — LIMIT does not short-circuit the gather, only the combine

commands.name: ZINTERSTORE
commands.syntax: ZINTERSTORE destination numkeys key [key ...] [WEIGHTS weight [weight ...]] [AGGREGATE SUM|MIN|MAX]
commands.summary: Store the intersection of the given sorted sets into destination.
commands.complexity: O(sum of the source cardinalities + R log R)

commands.name: ZPOPMIN
commands.summary: Pop up to count members with the lowest scores.
commands.complexity: O(M log N)

commands.name: ZPOPMIN.BELOW
commands.summary: kevy extension: pop up to count lowest members with score strictly below the threshold (delayed-job primitive).
commands.complexity: O(M log N) — take_while stops at the first score at or above the threshold, so it never walks past the due prefix
commands.compat: kevy-only: a delayed-job primitive (score = due time); no Redis analogue

commands.name: ZRANGE
commands.summary: Return members by rank range.
commands.complexity: O(log N + M) — one rank descent seeks to start, then the M requested members are walked
commands.compat: differs: only the legacy 'key start stop [WITHSCORES]' form is accepted — the Redis 6.2 BYSCORE / BYLEX / REV / LIMIT arguments are a syntax error

commands.name: ZRANGEBYSCORE
commands.syntax: ZRANGEBYSCORE key min max [WITHSCORES] [LIMIT offset count]
commands.summary: Return members with scores within the given bounds.
commands.complexity: O(log N + M) — a rank descent seeks to the score bound, then only the M in-range members are walked; LIMIT is still applied after the match set is materialised, so it bounds the reply, not the walk

commands.name: ZRANK
commands.summary: Return a member's rank, ordered from the lowest score.
commands.complexity: O(log N) — a hash lookup for the score, then one descent of the rank-augmented (score, member) tree
commands.compat: differs: the Redis 7.2 WITHSCORE option is not supported

commands.name: ZREM
commands.summary: Remove one or more members from a sorted set.
commands.complexity: O(M log N)

commands.name: ZREMRANGEBYRANK
commands.summary: Remove members within the given rank range.
commands.complexity: O(log N + M log N) — a rank descent seeks to start, then M member deletes

commands.name: ZREMRANGEBYSCORE
commands.summary: Remove members with scores within the given bounds.
commands.complexity: O(log N + M log N) — a seek finds the hit set, then M deletes

commands.name: ZREVRANGEBYSCORE
commands.syntax: ZREVRANGEBYSCORE key max min [WITHSCORES] [LIMIT offset count]
commands.summary: Return members with scores within the given bounds, highest first.
commands.complexity: O(log N + M) — a seeked forward walk of the M matches, then the result is reversed

commands.name: ZSCAN
commands.summary: Iterate a sorted set's members and scores (single-batch cursor).
commands.complexity: O(N) — the whole set is materialised
commands.compat: differs: not a cursor iterator — every call returns the whole set with cursor 0, and COUNT is parsed then ignored

commands.name: ZSCORE
commands.summary: Return a member's score.
commands.complexity: O(1) — a hash lookup

commands.name: ZUNIONSTORE
commands.syntax: ZUNIONSTORE destination numkeys key [key ...] [WEIGHTS weight [weight ...]] [AGGREGATE SUM|MIN|MAX]
commands.summary: Store the union of the given sorted sets into destination.
commands.complexity: O(sum of the source cardinalities + R log R)

commands.name: XACK
commands.summary: Acknowledge pending entries for a consumer group.
commands.complexity: O(A log P)

commands.name: XADD
commands.syntax: XADD key [NOMKSTREAM] [MAXLEN [=|~] threshold | MINID [=|~] id] id|* field value [field value ...]
commands.summary: Append an entry to a stream, with optional trim.
commands.complexity: O(log N) to insert; O(N*F) whenever a MAXLEN / MINID clause actually evicts, because the trim triggers a full weight recompute
commands.compat: differs: the approximate-trim '~' is accepted for wire compatibility but always trims exactly, and the LIMIT clause is not parsed

commands.name: XAUTOCLAIM
commands.syntax: XAUTOCLAIM key group consumer min-idle-time start [COUNT count] [JUSTID]
commands.summary: Scan and claim idle pending entries starting from a cursor.
commands.complexity: O(log P + K + COUNT log N); the idle filter runs before the take, so a PEL of fresh entries is walked in full
commands.compat: differs: the next-cursor is last-claimed+1 rather than 0-0 when the PEL scan completes, so a client looping until 0-0 needs one extra round trip

commands.name: XCLAIM
commands.syntax: XCLAIM key group consumer min-idle-time id [id ...] [IDLE ms] [TIME unix-time-milliseconds] [RETRYCOUNT count] [FORCE] [JUSTID]
commands.summary: Claim specific idle pending entries for a consumer.
commands.complexity: O(A * (log P + log N))
commands.compat: differs: IDLE / TIME / RETRYCOUNT / FORCE / JUSTID are parsed but LASTID is not, and a missing key or group returns 'no such key' instead of NOGROUP

commands.name: XDEL
commands.summary: Delete entries from a stream by ID.
commands.complexity: O(D log N + N*F) for D ids — NOT O(1): the trailing weight recompute is linear in the whole stream

commands.name: XGROUP
commands.syntax: XGROUP CREATE key group id|$ [MKSTREAM] | DESTROY key group | SETID key group id|$ | CREATECONSUMER key group consumer | DELCONSUMER key group consumer
commands.summary: Manage stream consumer groups.
commands.complexity: CREATE / DESTROY: O(1) plus an O(N*F) reweigh. SETID / CREATECONSUMER: O(1). DELCONSUMER: O(P)
commands.compat: differs: CREATE / SETID / DESTROY / CREATECONSUMER / DELCONSUMER / MKSTREAM are supported, but on a missing key the non-CREATE subcommands return 0 or NOGROUP instead of Redis's error, and XGROUP HELP is absent

commands.name: XINFO
commands.syntax: XINFO STREAM key | GROUPS key | CONSUMERS key group | HELP
commands.summary: Introspect a stream, its groups, or its consumers.
commands.complexity: STREAM: O(1). GROUPS: O(G*N) — 'lag' is a linear walk of every entry, once per group. CONSUMERS: O(C)
commands.compat: differs: STREAM / GROUPS / CONSUMERS / HELP only — XINFO STREAM FULL is absent; radix-tree-keys and nodes are synthetic (we have no radix tree), entries-read is approximated, and CONSUMERS omits 'inactive'

commands.name: XLEN
commands.summary: Return the number of entries in a stream.

commands.name: XPENDING
commands.syntax: XPENDING key group [[IDLE min-idle-time] start end count [consumer]]
commands.summary: Inspect pending entries of a consumer group (summary or extended form).
commands.complexity: summary: O(P*C) — the per-consumer tally is a linear find per PEL row. extended: O(log P + K)

commands.name: XRANGE
commands.summary: Return stream entries within an ID range.
commands.complexity: O(log N + M) — a B-tree range descent, COUNT applied lazily

commands.name: XREAD
commands.syntax: XREAD [COUNT count] [BLOCK milliseconds] STREAMS key [key ...] id [id ...]
commands.summary: Read new entries from one or more streams, optionally blocking.
commands.complexity: O(S * (log N + M)) over S streams; '$' is O(1); the park is O(1)
commands.compat: differs: the '+' last-id form is not parsed — only explicit IDs and '$' are accepted

commands.name: XREADGROUP
commands.syntax: XREADGROUP GROUP group consumer [COUNT count] [BLOCK milliseconds] [NOACK] STREAMS key [key ...] id [id ...]
commands.summary: Read stream entries as a consumer-group member, optionally blocking.
commands.complexity: '>' form: O(log N + U + M) — COUNT does NOT bound the scan, the entire undelivered tail is materialised first. Replay form: O(log P + K)
commands.compat: differs: COUNT is parsed but does not bound the '>' scan

commands.name: XREVRANGE
commands.summary: Return stream entries within an ID range, in reverse order.
commands.complexity: O(log N + M)

commands.name: XSETID
commands.summary: Overwrite a stream's last-generated ID and bookkeeping counters.
commands.complexity: O(log N)

commands.name: XTRIM
commands.summary: Trim a stream by length or minimum ID.
commands.complexity: O(R log N + N*F) for R evicted entries
commands.compat: differs: '~' is accepted but trimming is always exact, LIMIT is not parsed, and trailing tokens after the threshold are silently ignored instead of erroring

commands.name: GEOADD
commands.syntax: GEOADD key [NX|XX] [CH] longitude latitude member [longitude latitude member ...]
commands.summary: Add geospatial members (longitude/latitude) to a geo set.
commands.complexity: O(M log N); CH adds an O(M^2) term

commands.name: GEODIST
commands.summary: Return the distance between two geo members.

commands.name: GEOHASH
commands.summary: Return the base32 geohash string of each member.
commands.complexity: O(M)

commands.name: GEOPOS
commands.summary: Return the longitude/latitude of each member.
commands.complexity: O(M)

commands.name: GEORADIUS
commands.syntax: GEORADIUS key longitude latitude radius m|km|mi|ft [WITHCOORD] [WITHDIST] [WITHHASH] [COUNT count [ANY]] [ASC|DESC] [STORE key] [STOREDIST key]
commands.summary: Legacy radius search around a coordinate, with optional STORE writes.
commands.complexity: O(log N + C) — up to nine neighbour cell ranges, each seeked on the score tree; C = members inside the matched cells. STORE / STOREDIST add O(K log K) to write plus O(D) to clear the destination
commands.compat: differs: the destination is written on its own shard, so a STORE across shards is not atomic with the search

commands.name: GEORADIUSBYMEMBER
commands.syntax: GEORADIUSBYMEMBER key member radius m|km|mi|ft [WITHCOORD] [WITHDIST] [WITHHASH] [COUNT count [ANY]] [ASC|DESC] [STORE key] [STOREDIST key]
commands.summary: Legacy radius search around an existing member, with optional STORE writes.
commands.complexity: O(log N + C) — the seeked nine-cell fetch, same as GEORADIUS; the anchor lookup is O(1)
commands.compat: differs: the destination is written on its own shard, so a STORE across shards is not atomic with the search

commands.name: GEOSEARCH
commands.syntax: GEOSEARCH key FROMMEMBER member|FROMLONLAT longitude latitude BYRADIUS radius m|km|mi|ft|BYBOX width height m|km|mi|ft [ASC|DESC] [COUNT count [ANY]] [WITHCOORD] [WITHDIST] [WITHHASH]
commands.summary: Search members within a radius or box from a member or coordinate.
commands.complexity: O(log N + C) — up to nine neighbour ranges, each a seeked slice of the score tree; C = members inside the matched geohash cells (the block bound now prunes iteration too, not just distance maths)
commands.compat: differs: STOREDIST is accepted and ignored on the read-only form; COUNT 0 is an error

commands.name: GEOSEARCHSTORE
commands.syntax: GEOSEARCHSTORE destination source FROMMEMBER member|FROMLONLAT longitude latitude BYRADIUS radius m|km|mi|ft|BYBOX width height m|km|mi|ft [ASC|DESC] [COUNT count [ANY]] [STOREDIST]
commands.summary: Run GEOSEARCH on source and store the hits into destination.
commands.complexity: O(log N + C) to search, plus O(D + K log K) to rewrite the destination on its own shard
commands.compat: differs: STOREDIST stores the distance in the unit the query asked for (Redis does the same); the destination is written on its own shard, so the source and destination may live on different cores and the write is not atomic with the read

commands.name: ECHO
commands.summary: Return the given message.

commands.name: HELLO
commands.summary: Handshake: report server info and switch RESP protocol version (2 or 3).
commands.compat: differs: only HELLO [2|3] is honoured — the AUTH and SETNAME tails are parsed off and ignored, because kevy has no AUTH and this form does not set the connection name

commands.name: PING
commands.summary: Ping the server; returns PONG or echoes the optional message.
commands.compat: differs: kevy has no RESP2 subscriber mode, so PING while subscribed does not switch to the array form and non-pubsub commands stay legal on a subscribed connection

commands.name: QUIT
commands.summary: Close the connection after replying OK.

commands.name: SELECT
commands.summary: Select the logical database; kevy is single-DB and only accepts index 0.
commands.compat: differs: kevy is single-DB — SELECT 0 replies OK and any other index is an error

commands.name: BGREWRITEAOF
commands.summary: Start an append-only-file rewrite in the background.
commands.complexity: O(S) fan-out; each shard freezes a copy-on-write view and hands serialise plus fsync to its own worker
commands.compat: differs: replies +OK rather than Redis's status line, rewrites one AOF per shard, and replies +OK even when AOF is disabled

commands.name: BGSAVE
commands.summary: Start a snapshot save in the background.
commands.complexity: O(S) fan-out; O(N/S) copy-on-write freeze per shard on the reactor, then serialise off-thread
commands.compat: differs: replies +OK rather than Redis's status line, and writes one dump per shard

commands.name: COMMAND
commands.summary: Introspect the command table (COUNT, LIST, INFO, DOCS subcommands).
commands.complexity: bare / LIST / DOCS: O(V) verbs. COUNT: O(1). INFO / DOCS with k names: O(k*V) — the lookup is a linear scan
commands.compat: differs: COUNT / LIST / INFO / DOCS only — GETKEYS and GETKEYSANDFLAGS are absent, and the info rows hard-code first/last/step and leave ACL categories, tips and key-specs empty

commands.name: CONFIG
commands.syntax: CONFIG GET parameter | SET parameter value | REWRITE | RESETSTAT
commands.summary: Read or change server configuration parameters.
commands.complexity: GET: O(patterns * 16). SET: O(1) plus one config swap that shards pick up on their next tick. REWRITE: O(config file size)
commands.compat: differs: 16 Redis-named parameters exist; only maxmemory, maxmemory-policy, appendfsync, the auto-rewrite pair, hz, maxmemory-samples, loglevel and logfile are hot-settable — bind, port, io-threads, dir and appendonly error at runtime; RESETSTAT is a no-op

commands.name: CLIENT
commands.syntax: CLIENT ID | GETNAME | SETNAME name | LIST | KILL filter | INFO | NO-EVICT ON|OFF
commands.summary: Connection introspection and control subcommands.
commands.complexity: ID / GETNAME / SETNAME / INFO: O(1). LIST: O(S) fan-out + O(C) rows. KILL: O(S) + O(C) scan
commands.compat: differs: ID / GETNAME / SETNAME / INFO / LIST (bare) / KILL (ID, ADDR) / NO-EVICT only; CLIENT LIST with a filter is a syntax error and every other subcommand (PAUSE, REPLY, TRACKING, UNBLOCK, NO-TOUCH) is unknown

commands.name: CLUSTER
commands.syntax: CLUSTER INFO | NODES | SLOTS | SHARDS | KEYSLOT key | COUNTKEYSINSLOT slot
commands.summary: Cluster topology introspection (virtual-node model over shards).
commands.complexity: INFO / NODES / SLOTS / SHARDS / MYID: O(S). KEYSLOT: O(len(key)). COUNTKEYSINSLOT: O(N/S)
commands.compat: differs: a read-only virtual-node topology derived from config (one virtual master per shard) — no gossip, no MEET / FORGET / SETSLOT effect (they reply OK as no-ops), no MIGRATE / ASK, no failover; COUNTKEYSINSLOT counts only the answering shard's keys

commands.name: DBSIZE
commands.summary: Return the number of keys across all shards.
commands.complexity: O(S) — one message per shard, each answering O(1) from its map length; NOT O(N)

commands.name: DEBUG
commands.summary: Debug subcommands; SLEEP blocks the shard, other subcommands are tolerated as OK.
commands.complexity: SLEEP: parks the ANSWERING shard's reactor thread for the duration (other shards keep serving). Everything else: O(1)
commands.compat: differs: SLEEP is the only subcommand with an effect and it blocks one shard, not the server; every other subcommand is accepted and answered OK without doing anything

commands.name: FLUSHALL
commands.summary: Delete every key on every shard.
commands.complexity: O(S) fan-out; per shard O(N/S) clear plus WATCH invalidation plus a feed-generation bump
commands.compat: differs: ASYNC / SYNC are accepted and ignored (the flush is always synchronous per shard), and it bumps the CDC feed generation, so live FEED cursors get a resync error

commands.name: FLUSHDB
commands.summary: Delete every key of the current database (kevy is single-DB: same as FLUSHALL).
commands.complexity: O(N + S) — identical to FLUSHALL
commands.compat: differs: kevy is single-DB, so FLUSHDB is an alias of FLUSHALL; ASYNC / SYNC are ignored

commands.name: INFO
commands.summary: Report server statistics and status sections as text.
commands.complexity: O(1) in the keyspace — it never walks it; O(S) to sum the per-shard gauges
commands.compat: differs: 8 sections only (server, clients, memory, persistence, stats, replication, cluster, keyspace) — no commandstats / latencystats / errorstats / cpu; reports redis_version 7.4.0 for client sniffing plus a kevy_version line, and the values are up to one tick stale

commands.name: MEMORY
commands.syntax: MEMORY USAGE key [SAMPLES count] | STATS | DOCTOR | PURGE | MALLOC-STATS
commands.summary: Memory introspection subcommands.
commands.complexity: USAGE: O(1) — the accounting is exact, not sampled. STATS: O(1) from the instance-wide gauges
commands.compat: differs: USAGE's SAMPLES count is parsed and ignored (our accounting is exact); PURGE is a no-op (system allocator, no arena); DOCTOR and MALLOC-STATS return canned strings; STATS is a trimmed 8-field set

commands.name: SAVE
commands.summary: Synchronously snapshot the dataset to disk.
commands.complexity: O(S) fan-out; O(N/S) copy-on-write freeze per shard
commands.compat: differs: SAVE is no longer synchronous-until-durable — it freezes a copy-on-write view and replies OK immediately, so 'SAVE returned, therefore the dump is safe to copy' no longer holds

commands.name: SHUTDOWN
commands.summary: Stop the server process (connection drops without a reply).
commands.complexity: O(1) to trip the stop flag; the drain that follows is O(N)
commands.compat: differs: only SHUTDOWN [NOSAVE|SAVE] parses — NOW, FORCE and ABORT are a syntax error

commands.name: SLOWLOG
commands.summary: Inspect or reset the slow-command log.
commands.complexity: GET: O(S) fan-out plus O(L log L) to merge. LEN: O(S). RESET: O(S)
commands.compat: differs: the log is per-shard and GET merges across shards by timestamp, so ids are not globally monotonic; every entry's client-addr and client-name are empty strings

commands.name: FAILOVER
commands.summary: Planned zero-loss handover: quiesce writes, wait for the target replica to drain, promote it, and follow it.
commands.complexity: O(1) at the command — the handover runs in the background, polling the target until it is caught up
commands.compat: differs: Redis's syntax is FAILOVER [TO host port [FORCE]] [ABORT] [TIMEOUT ms] with an optional target; kevy's is FAILOVER host port [TIMEOUT ms] | ABORT — the target is mandatory and positional, and the port given is the target's client port

commands.name: REPL.TOKEN
commands.summary: kevy extension: mint a read-your-writes token — per-shard [generation, offset] pairs (a primary reports its live feed tail; a replica its applied positions).
commands.complexity: O(S) — one (generation, offset) pair per shard
commands.compat: kevy-only: the read-your-writes token; the nearest Redis concept is master_repl_offset, which is not a resumable per-shard cursor

commands.name: REPL.WAIT
commands.summary: kevy extension: on a replica, block until every shard has applied the given REPL.TOKEN (then reads are read-your-writes); +OK on success, -MISDIRECTED writer is <primary> on timeout or generation mismatch. Default TIMEOUT 1000 ms, hard cap 60 s. On a primary: immediate +OK.
commands.complexity: O(S) — a barrier, not a keyspace op; the wall-clock cost is the replication lag, bounded by TIMEOUT (default 1s, hard-capped at 60s)
commands.compat: kevy-only: waits until a (generation, offset) token has been applied, which is what makes read-your-writes possible across a failover

commands.name: REPLICAOF
commands.summary: Make this server a replica of another, or promote it with NO ONE.
commands.complexity: O(1) at the command; the full resync that follows is O(N) in the background
commands.compat: differs: the port argument is the primary's REPLICATION port base, not its client port (the default base is client port + 10000); chain replication is rejected

commands.name: ROLE
commands.summary: Report the replication role and state of this server.
commands.complexity: O(1) on a replica; O(R) on a primary

commands.name: SLAVEOF
commands.summary: Legacy alias of REPLICAOF.
commands.complexity: O(1) plus a background resync
commands.compat: differs: a deprecated alias of REPLICAOF, including the replication-port-base argument

commands.name: WAIT
commands.summary: Block until every shard's master_repl_offset is acknowledged by at least numreplicas replicas (or timeout ms pass); returns the minimum acked-replica count across shards. timeout 0 = wait forever, hard-capped at 60 s. NOTE: a replica ACK is not fsync durability.
commands.complexity: O(S) — an all-shard barrier returning the MINIMUM acked-replica count; the wall-clock cost is the replication round trip
commands.compat: differs: it is an all-shard barrier returning the minimum across shards (Redis has one offset to wait on); timeout 0 is capped at 60s rather than blocking forever, and an ACK means the frame reached the replica's apply pipeline, not fsync durability

commands.name: DISCARD
commands.summary: Abort the open MULTI transaction.
commands.complexity: O(1) — drops the queued commands and the WATCH set

commands.name: EXEC
commands.summary: Execute every command queued since MULTI.
commands.complexity: O(sum of the queued commands' costs); with W watched keys, one extra O(W) pre-check fanned into O(min(W,S)) messages
commands.compat: differs: a MULTI batch spanning several shards is per-shard-atomic, not globally isolated (there is no cross-shard snapshot); a queue-time error aborts the whole batch with EXECABORT, but a runtime error inside EXEC leaves the other commands applied, as in Redis

commands.name: MULTI
commands.summary: Start a transaction; subsequent commands are queued until EXEC.

commands.name: UNWATCH
commands.summary: Forget all watched keys.

commands.name: WATCH
commands.summary: Watch keys for optimistic locking of the next EXEC.
commands.complexity: O(W) keys, grouped into O(min(W,S)) cross-shard messages

commands.name: PSUBSCRIBE
commands.summary: Subscribe to channels matching the given glob patterns.
commands.complexity: O(p * P) — each pattern costs a linear scan of the shared pattern registry

commands.name: PUBLISH
commands.summary: Post a message to a channel; returns the receiver count.
commands.complexity: O(1) channel lookup + O(P) — a linear walk of the registered patterns with one glob match each, even when none match. Delivery fans out only to the shards holding a subscriber

commands.name: PUNSUBSCRIBE
commands.summary: Unsubscribe from patterns (all patterns when none given).
commands.complexity: O(p * P)

commands.name: SUBSCRIBE
commands.summary: Subscribe to the given channels.
commands.complexity: O(c) channels; never fans out to other shards
commands.compat: differs: kevy has no RESP2 subscriber mode — after SUBSCRIBE the connection may still issue any command, where Redis restricts it to the pubsub verbs plus PING / QUIT / RESET

commands.name: UNSUBSCRIBE
commands.summary: Unsubscribe from channels (all channels when none given).
commands.complexity: O(c) channels

commands.name: EVAL
commands.summary: Run a Lua script server-side; routed to KEYS[1]'s shard when numkeys >= 1.
commands.complexity: O(compile + the script's own work). The whole script is one atomic unit on KEYS[1]'s shard and blocks that shard for its duration. The runaway guard is an INSTRUCTION budget (lua time_limit_ms x 40000 instructions), not a wall clock
commands.compat: differs: there is no -BUSY state and no SCRIPT KILL — an over-budget script is aborted in place and answered with an ordinary error; nested EVAL is rejected, a redis.call touching another shard's key returns CROSSSLOT, and EVAL auto-caches its source by SHA1 so EVALSHA works without SCRIPT LOAD

commands.name: EVALSHA
commands.summary: Run a cached Lua script by its SHA1 digest.
commands.complexity: O(1) cache lookup, then identical to EVAL
commands.compat: differs: same instruction-budget model as EVAL (no -BUSY, no SCRIPT KILL); the cache is process-wide and EVAL populates it

commands.name: SCRIPT
commands.syntax: SCRIPT LOAD script | EXISTS sha1 [sha1 ...] | FLUSH [ASYNC|SYNC]
commands.summary: Manage the process-wide Lua script cache.
commands.complexity: LOAD: O(len(script)). EXISTS: O(k). FLUSH: O(cached scripts)
commands.compat: differs: LOAD / EXISTS / FLUSH only — SCRIPT KILL does not exist, by design: there is no -BUSY state to interrupt because an over-budget script self-aborts

commands.name: IDX.COUNT
commands.syntax: IDX.COUNT name RANGE min max | EQ value
commands.summary: Count index entries matching a range or equality predicate.
commands.complexity: O(log N + matched) per shard — NOT an O(1) counter and not a B-tree rank query; it counts the matched range
commands.compat: kevy-only: nearest is FT.SEARCH with LIMIT 0 0

commands.name: IDX.CREATE
commands.syntax: IDX.CREATE name ON PREFIX prefix FIELD field TYPE i64|f64|str|vector KIND range|unique|text|ann|agg [MAXMEM bytes] [DIM dim] [DISTANCE cosine|l2|ip] [M m] [EF ef] [GROUPBY field]
commands.summary: Declare a secondary index over a key prefix (catalog mutation, sidecar-persisted).
commands.complexity: O(1) at the call; the build is asynchronous — each shard snapshots its matching keys (O(keys on that shard)) then backfills 2048 rows per tick. Per-row build cost: range/unique O(log N), text O(tokens), vector O(ef_construction * M * dim)
commands.compat: kevy-only: nearest is RediSearch FT.CREATE — comparable declarative index-on-prefix, but RediSearch is a separate module with its own index server; kevy's catalog is in-process and the index is maintained in the write hook

commands.name: IDX.DROP
commands.summary: Drop a declared index (catalog mutation, sidecar-persisted).
commands.complexity: O(catalog size)

commands.name: IDX.LIST
commands.summary: List declared indexes with per-index build state and stats.
commands.complexity: Not O(1) — per shard, per index it computes live stats: range/unique O(1), text O(distinct tokens + docs), vector O(nodes + links), agg O(groups + rows)
commands.compat: kevy-only: nearest is FT._LIST plus FT.INFO combined

commands.name: IDX.EXPLAIN
commands.syntax: IDX.EXPLAIN name RANGE min max|EQ value|MATCH text|KNN vector|GROUPS [args ...]
commands.summary: The IDX.QUERY parse without the execution: kind, state, est_rows, and the plan line.
commands.complexity: The plan is parse-only, but est_rows costs the same live stats walk as IDX.LIST
commands.compat: kevy-only: nearest is FT.EXPLAIN, which returns a parsed query tree; ours returns kind, build state, estimated rows and a one-line plan

commands.name: IDX.QUERY
commands.syntax: IDX.QUERY name RANGE min max [LIMIT n] [CURSOR c] [FIELDS field ...] | name EQ value [LIMIT n] [CURSOR c] [FIELDS field ...] | name MATCH text [LIMIT n] [FIELDS field ...] | name KNN vector [LIMIT k] [EF ef] [FIELDS field ...] | name GROUP group | name GROUPS [BY count|sum|min|max] [LIMIT n] | HYBRID text_idx MATCH text ann_idx KNN vector [LIMIT n] [RRFK k] [EF ef] [FIELDS field ...] | COMPOSE AND|OR nameA RANGE min max|EQ value nameB RANGE min max|EQ value [LIMIT n] [CURSOR c] [FIELDS field ...]
commands.summary: Query an index: range/equality, text MATCH, vector KNN, aggregation groups, or a two-index COMPOSE.
commands.complexity: Depends on the index kind. range: O(log N + limit). unique: O(log N + hits). full-text: O(sum of the posting lists), MaxScore-pruned. vector ANN: O(dim * (M log N + ef * M)) distance evaluations (HNSW). agg GROUPS: a bounded top-K with 1 to 3 fan-out rounds. HYBRID: both sub-queries at 4x depth, fused by RRF at the origin. COMPOSE: NOT limit-bounded — both leaves are materialised in full, because the result is key-ordered while a segment is value-ordered
commands.compat: kevy-only: nearest is RediSearch FT.SEARCH — genuinely comparable on two axes (our text index is BM25 over inverted segments, our vector index is HNSW, and RediSearch offers both). Differences: no separate module or index server; our BM25 statistics are per-shard, not global; and our query surface is a fixed grammar, not a DSL — no field boosting, no phrase or proximity search, no stemming, no aggregation pipeline

commands.name: IDX.REBUILD
commands.summary: Rebuild an ANN index (tombstone compaction).
commands.complexity: Vector indexes only (tombstone compaction). O(V_live * ef_construction * M * dim) distance evaluations, on every shard, synchronously — the most expensive verb in the extension surface
commands.compat: kevy-only: no Redis analogue — RediSearch handles HNSW deletes internally and exposes no rebuild verb

commands.name: IDX.VERIFY
commands.summary: Verify an index: re-read every held entry against its row and report entries/bytes/coerce_failures/duplicates/drift/checked.
commands.complexity: O(N) per shard — every held entry is re-read against its row and re-coerced, which is the point: it makes index drift falsifiable rather than merely asserted
commands.compat: kevy-only: no Redis analogue — RediSearch's index is asynchronously maintained and offers no consistency-verify verb

commands.name: VIEW.CREATE
commands.syntax: VIEW.CREATE name QUERY tree ORDER BY index [DESC] [MODE virtual|materialized] [TOPK k] [VIA template] (tree = '( AND|OR|DIFF sub sub )' | 'index RANGE min max' | 'index EQ value')
commands.summary: Declare a composed view over indexes with an ORDER BY (catalog mutation, sidecar-persisted).
commands.complexity: O(tree size) at the call. A materialized view builds lazily on the next tick (a full eval_tree plus an O(M log M) sort); a virtual view builds nothing, ever
commands.compat: kevy-only: no Redis analogue. A view is neither a stored query nor a join — it is a named composition tree over declared indexes that stores membership and order only, never field values

commands.name: VIEW.DROP
commands.summary: Drop a declared view (catalog mutation, sidecar-persisted).
commands.complexity: O(catalog size)

commands.name: VIEW.EXPLAIN
commands.summary: Explain a view's composition tree with per-leaf cardinalities.
commands.complexity: O(sum over leaves of (log N + matched)) — each leaf's cardinality is a real count, so EXPLAIN on a broad leaf costs as much as counting it
commands.compat: kevy-only: nearest is FT.EXPLAIN, which returns a query tree rather than per-leaf cardinalities

commands.name: VIEW.LIST
commands.summary: List declared views with their mode and shape.
commands.complexity: O(views) at the origin — the catalog is process-global

commands.name: VIEW.QUERY
commands.summary: Page through a view's ordered members, optionally hydrating fields via the VIA template.
commands.complexity: virtual: O(log N_order + candidates * leaves) — it streams the ORDER index and probes membership per candidate, stopping at the limit, so it never materialises the member set. materialized: O(log M + limit). Adding FIELDS with VIA costs a SECOND fan-out to hydrate the rows
commands.compat: kevy-only: no Redis analogue. Absent by construction: no joins, no predicates at the view layer, no projection from the view itself, no HAVING, no aggregation

commands.name: VIEW.REBUILD
commands.summary: Force a rebuild of a materialized view.
commands.complexity: Materialized only. A full eval_tree over the whole tree plus an O(M log M) sort and re-insert, on every shard, now (not deferred to a tick)

commands.name: VIEW.VERIFY
commands.summary: Verify a view and report member/byte statistics.
commands.complexity: materialized: O(M). virtual: O(sum over leaves of (log N + leaf range) + M) — a full fresh evaluation just to report cardinality, which is the one place a virtual view is the expensive one

commands.name: FEED.READ
commands.syntax: FEED.READ shard generation offset [COUNT n] [PREFIX prefix ...]
commands.summary: Read change-feed frames from one shard past a generation/offset cursor.
commands.complexity: A single shard (the shard is an argument, not a fan-out). O(log B) to locate the start offset in the backlog plus O(count * frame size) to decode and re-encode. COUNT defaults to 256 and is hard-capped at 4096
commands.compat: kevy-only: no clean Redis analogue. Keyspace notifications are fire-and-forget with no cursor and no replay; Redis Streams have cursors but are a stream you must dual-write to, not a feed over your existing keyspace; the replication backlog is what this is built on, but Redis exposes it only to replicas. kevy is deliberately not a broker: no consumer groups, no server-side positions, no global cross-shard order

commands.name: FEED.SHARDS
commands.summary: Return the number of change-feed shards.
commands.complexity: O(1), answered locally
commands.compat: kevy-only: Redis has no shard-partitioned change feed to enumerate

commands.name: FEED.TAIL
commands.summary: Return a shard's current feed generation and next offset.
commands.complexity: O(1) on a single shard
commands.compat: kevy-only: nearest is INFO replication's master_repl_offset, which is not a resumable per-shard CDC cursor

commands.name: PREFIX.STATS
commands.summary: Report key-count and byte statistics for a key prefix.
commands.complexity: O(keys on the shard) — a full keyspace walk on every shard; the prefix cannot be precomputed
commands.compat: kevy-only: nearest is INFO keyspace's db0:keys=N,expires=M — the same two counters, but whole-DB and O(1) off a counter, where ours is per-prefix and therefore O(keyspace)

commands.name: PREFIX.DIGEST
commands.summary: Order-insensitive checksum of a prefix's rows for migration verification.
commands.complexity: O(keys on the shard) to walk plus O(sum of row sizes) to digest, on every shard. Per-row digests XOR together, so the result is order-insensitive and safe across shard counts
commands.compat: kevy-only: nearest is DEBUG DIGEST — comparable in kind (Redis also XORs per-key digests), but Redis's is whole-DB and lives behind DEBUG, while ours is per-prefix (the unit a migration actually cares about) and is a supported verb
